#### 1. cholestasis, intrahepatic, of pregnancy, 3  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.784)

Loss-of-function mutations in ABCB4 disrupt normal phospholipid transport, leading to cholestasis, which manifests as progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis in type 3 and intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy in type 3.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in ABCB4 who do not exhibit any signs or symptoms of cholestasis, or conversely, individuals with cholestasis and related phenotypes who do not carry pathogenic variants in ABCB4. _(variant: Exome Allele Frequency > 0.001 for known pathogenic variants)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving ABCB4 and phospholipid transport in both diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies that restore or enhance the function of the MDR3 transporter, potentially benefiting patients with both conditions.
